author: DamiLee
description:
The most legendary city in Middle-earth might also be the most miserable place to actually live in.

Minas Tirith looks perfect on paper. Seven levels of white stone, built into the mountain, basically unbreakable. But what happens when the war ends and someone just needs to deliver bread?

Every loaf, every message, every emergency has to weave through switchbacks across the entire ridge. Even with pulleys and lifts, the logistics alone would be exhausting. And that is before you factor in what the city quietly tells you about where you stand.

The rich live at the top, close to power, close to the citadel, and furthest from danger. The poor live at the bottom, right where the killing grounds begin. The very design of the city encodes a social hierarchy into its stone.

So here is the contradiction nobody talks about. It is majestic, but suffocating. Impenetrable, but isolated. The perfect fortress, and somehow the worst city.

Great during a war. A logistical nightmare during peace.
title: Minas Tirith Is the Best Fortress, But Worst City in Middle-earth
